Subject: Rack affinity & slot commitment for Aurelia (AUR-7723)

Hi team,

Aurelia (deal AUR-7723) is in final legal review and they asked for a firm note on rack-affinity constraints and a short-term slot commitment for the first 90 days of production. Key ask from the customer: guarantee access to 64 A100-equivalent GPUs starting 2028-09-01 with a fallback plan if we hit thermal binning issues.

Can ops validate the following by EOD Pacific today?
- Rack-level availability: contiguous racks vs spread allocation for 64 GPUs
- Thermal binning implications for 40+ sustained token/sec workloads
- Recommended soft-hold duration and approval gate (30/14/7 days?)
- Any SLA exception required for guaranteed start date

I attached their one-pager (Aurelia_MVP_capacity_request.pdf). Elena — feel free to add if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Tessa

Subject: Re: Rack affinity & slot commitment for Aurelia (AUR-7723)

Tessa — quick inventory note. Ran a physical-to-logical mapping against the fleet:
- We have three candidate PODs that can supply A100-equivalent slices. Each POD has 12 usable A100-equivalent cards due to current binning (12 x 3 = 36 per contiguous zone).
- To hit 64 GPUs with rack affinity, we need to span at least 3 racks (36 + 28 from adjacent rack) — contiguous allocation is tight.
- Thermal note: two racks show higher ambient temps (hot aisle 3). We can schedule a thermal-aware placement that keeps sustained jobs on the cooler racks but that reduces contiguous density.

Prod proposal: soft-hold 72 GPUs across these racks for 14 days while legal/procurement finalizes. That gives a 10% buffer and avoids immediate preemption for other late-stage deals. I attached a snapshot.

Next question: do we require a signed commitment (DocuSign link) before we mark the hold? If yes, I recommend 14-day soft-hold + 7-day firm hold after signature.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Capacity Planner, Platform Operations

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Rack affinity & slot commitment for Aurelia (AUR-7723)

Adding a few operational constraints from runbooks and SLA perspective: 
- We can support a guaranteed start date, but it triggers an SLA exception for thermal risk if they insist on contiguous racks in the hot-aisle zone. Recommend spacing across 4 racks and using KV cache pre-warm to meet latency targets.
- If we accept the 14-day soft-hold Ben suggested, Ops will enforce a capacity-release alarm with automated notification to sales at T-3 days before auto-release. I can sign off on a 14-day soft-hold + 21-day contingency hold for an additional fee.
- For failover: propose fallback to quantized LLM variant with lower memory per-GPU in the event of binning-induced capacity shortfall. We should include that in the mutual action plan.

Approve soft-hold? I will file the org-level exception if so.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity & Supply, Redwood Inference
